name: ab_drain_engine
description: Indexer A/B drain scenario (engine): a 25-agent Linux fleet replays the syslog sample 4 times at 400 events/s per agent, 100,000 events (25 x 1,000 lines x 4) in about 10 s. ab_indexer.sh pauses the indexer for the whole run and resumes it afterwards, so the documents the manager accumulated are the fixed backlog whose drain (documents/s and time to drain, measured at the indexer) is the capacity of the manager's indexer sender. SIZING: the backlog must fit BOTH queues (analysisd.indexer_queue_max_bytes = 1 GiB on both sides, ab_options/*.conf) so that nothing is dropped on either side (indexer.events.dropped = 0; the A/B then compares the fraction of the accepted events each side indexed). v2 charges every event payload + RESULT_RESERVE_BYTES (2048): 100,000 x (payload + 2,048) <= 536,870,912 (half the quota) holds while payload <= 3,320 bytes (an enriched syslog event is about 1 to 2 KiB; at an assumed 3 KiB, v2 100,000 x 5,120 B = 512 MB, 47.7 % of the quota; v1 charges the payload only, 307 MB). The drain lasts several seconds at the indexer's pace, long enough for the 1 s probe. Do not raise repeat_count or agents without redoing this sum (README, 'Sizing the drain backlog').
